Subject: Checkpoint: Incident Action Roster & QBR readiness

Team — bringing together a short, actionable view of the incident from 2027-03-08 that impacted Acme Cloud (token-cache evictions -> sustained tail latency -> ~6% SLA misses for a 20-minute window). This thread is to: (1) confirm owners for each action, (2) produce a one-pager for QBR, and (3) lock the customer-facing credit proposal.

High-level timeline (short):
- 2027-03-08 02:14 UTC: sudden KV cache thrash after a bad model rollout (increased sequence length distribution)
- 02:20 UTC: autoscaler reacted; burst capacity engaged but routing lag caused queuing
- 02:34–02:54 UTC: elevated p50/p95 latency; total SLA misses ~6% for Acme's production traffic

Immediate actions (attached roster v1):
1) Stabilize kernel selection + pin model variant — owner: Markus Klein — ETA: 2027-03-11
2) KV cache tuning and short-term cache warmers — owner: Neha Kapoor — ETA: 2027-03-12
3) Autoscaler policy adjustment (burst thresholds) — owner: Marissa Cole — ETA: 2027-03-10
4) Customer communication + credit proposal — owner: Connor O'Brien — ETA: 2027-03-12
5) Postmortem doc + QBR blurb (one-paragraph + two metrics) — owner: Laura Bennett — ETA: 2027-03-11

Attachments: incident_action_roster.csv (action table), sla-impact-summary.xlsx (metric slices). Please review owners/ETAs and reply with confirmations or edits by end-of-day PDT today. I will consolidate for Laura's QBR slide pack.

Connor O'Brien
Director, Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference

Attached: incident_action_roster.csv (v2) and sla-impact-summary.xlsx (v2). I updated owners/ETAs per Marissa's note and added the metric gating task for rollout safety. Draft executive blurb below — please sign off or propose edits: 

Executive blurb (draft, ~100 words):
On 2027-03-08 a model rollout produced an unexpected shift in request token distribution that led to KV cache evictions and elevated tail latency for a short window. Our team engaged autoscaling and routing fallbacks; we limited customer-facing impact to a 20-minute period with an estimated 6% SLA miss for Acme's traffic. Immediate mitigations were implemented (pin model variant, cache warmers, autoscaler policy change). Next steps include permanent metric gating for rollouts and a follow-up software release with kernel-selection safeguards. We recommend a 5% usage credit to Acme pending final token-volume reconciliation.

Action items now: please update status (green/yellow/red) in the roster and return by EOD Monday. I will convert the blurb into a PNG for Laura's deck.

Connor O'Brien
Director, Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference
